A LITTLE CONTEXT

How to convert an image to Base64

Choose a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP file, then select the output you need: a complete data URL, raw Base64, an HTML image tag or a CSS background declaration. Copy the result or download it as text. The conversion runs in your browser and keeps the original image bytes.

Base64 length = 4 × ceil(original byte count ÷ 3)

References: RFC 4648: Base64 · RFC 2397: Data URLs

Good to know

What is the difference between raw Base64 and a data URL?

Raw Base64 contains only the encoded bytes. A data URL adds a media type and the ;base64, prefix, for example data:image/png;base64,. HTML and CSS image references need that complete URL, not just the raw payload.

Does Base64 compress or convert the image?

No. Base64 represents the original bytes as text. For larger files it adds roughly one third to the byte count, plus the data URL prefix. A JPEG remains JPEG; changing an extension does not convert its format.

Which images can I encode?

PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP are supported. The file limit is 10,485,760 bytes and the preview limit is 40 megapixels. The byte signature and the browser image decoder must both accept the image. SVG is not supported.

Can I convert an image URL directly?

This tool reads local files you select or drop. It does not fetch remote image URLs. Save the image to your device, then choose that file here.

Does my image get uploaded?

The image bytes are read and encoded on your device. Tool inputs are not sent to a conversion API. The website itself still makes normal requests to load its pages, scripts and local examples.

PRACTICAL REFERENCE

Use image Base64 in HTML, CSS and API fields

A Base64 payload and a complete image URL serve different purposes. Choose the format expected by the destination.

  1. Choose an image or try one of the complete PNG, JPEG or WebP examples above.
  2. Keep Data URL selected for an HTML/CSS image reference, or choose Raw Base64 when an API expects only the payload.
  3. Copy the full output or select Download output. The preview reports the detected format, dimensions and original byte count.

Replace the placeholder with the complete Data URL output, including its data:image/...;base64, prefix. The sample buttons above produce complete, working values. Copying the HTML output starts with an empty alt attribute; add an appropriate description when you use the image.

PRACTICAL REFERENCE

Image to Base64 troubleshooting

Encoding changes how bytes are represented. It does not repair corrupt images, convert formats or make a large payload smaller.

The file cannot be encoded

Check that it is a valid PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP within the size and preview limits. A renamed file can have a different byte format; output uses the detected format rather than trusting its extension.

My copied image does not display

Use the complete Data URL in an image src or CSS url(). Raw Base64 needs the media-type prefix before a browser can use it as an image URL. The destination may also restrict data: images through its content security policy.

Why did the output get larger?

Base64 maps each three input bytes to four text characters, with padding when needed. An original 3,000-byte image produces 4,000 Base64 characters before its data URL prefix. Use a normal image file URL when inline text is unsuitable.

I need to decode an image instead

Open the Base64 to image converter to paste an existing value, preview its bytes and download the original image. For UTF-8 text, use the Base64 decoder and encoder.
